title: fix(ci): make manual messaging token checks read-only
body:
## Summary and scope

Approved follow-up to #333, which was merged by another actor. This PR makes the existing manual messaging `action=check` genuinely read-only. Do not merge or enable auto-merge as part of this task.

- Original CI-audit main: `17a33eca11d585d84435af85340beece9b51d14e`.
- Follow-up baseline main: `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b`.
- Branch: `fix/ci-messaging-readonly-20260915`.
- Current main, merged into this branch without rewriting history: `52b32e4c17b3b0485c66e666137f85d44cc962d4` (externally merged artwork fix #369).
- Final branch SHA: `75c096bea71dbf58f92852fca3ab140116e6697f`. All five applicable hosted workflows below completed successfully on this exact SHA; results on the previous SHA do not substitute for this commit.
- PR: https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/370 — OPEN, MERGEABLE, auto-merge disabled. The previous `17c37ee72ff9924b3b153e2cb67bfd6c305b7101` approval was dismissed after synchronization and the documentation update; GitHub now reports REVIEW_REQUIRED. No PR merge was performed.

## Root cause and fix

The workflow's `check` and `refresh` branches both invoked the same no-argument command. That command could exchange tokens and call `flyctl secrets set` when either token failed validation or neared expiration. It also ignored CLI arguments, so adding `--check` only at the call site would not have been safe.

The script now parses an explicit `--check` flag, rejects ambiguous/unknown arguments before external calls, and returns a failing exit code when read-only inspection identifies required maintenance. This branch cannot reach token exchange, replacement Page-token lookup or Fly updates. The existing no-argument maintenance behavior and its failure exits are retained for hourly schedules and manual `refresh`.

The workflow validates the event/action before credential-bearing steps. Manual `check` receives only the Meta inspector and messaging-token secrets. Fly installation and `FLY_API_TOKEN` remain available only to the existing maintenance path. GitHub token permissions are explicitly `contents: read`. No secret values or dummy live credentials are introduced.

## Before / after

| Check | Before | Follow-up validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manual messaging check | Could exchange credentials and update Fly; unsafe for audit-only dispatch | [SUCCESS](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983634952) on the final SHA: Fly installation and credential maintenance were skipped; no refresh occurred |
| Scheduled/manual refresh | Refreshed only when needed, then verified | Same behavior retained and regression-tested; no mutating branch dispatch requested. The normal [main schedule](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34978706973) also passed on `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b` |
| Token regression suite | 14 tests | 24 tests passed, including all 16 two-token validity/expiry combinations, invalid/missing-token paths, CLI parsing, refresh errors and executable workflow action routing |
| Repository quality / formal / release / pipeline checks | Enforced existing suite | `npm run quality:repo` passed locally after main synchronization; [fresh CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983585477) and aggregate quality gate passed |
| Catalog authority | 1,108 reviewed candidates | Strict local audit and [fresh CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983585461) passed: 1,111 reviewed, zero unreviewed/stale; one follow-up fixture individually reviewed, plus two existing main artwork decisions preserved |
| Dependency security | Existing WebTorrent/IP exception | Unchanged policy passed; four high-severity dependency nodes remain allowlisted, not zero advisories |
| Safe install / production UI build | Existing required validation | [SUCCESS](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983585644): 208 suites / 1,981 UI tests passed, production build passed with five preloads / 357,571 bytes gzip initial JS |
| Persona journeys | Existing browser/device coverage | [SUCCESS](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983585477): 46 passed / 10 designed project-dedup skips |
| Datadog | Existing substantive configured checks | [SUCCESS](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34983585376) on the final branch SHA |

## Files changed

- `scripts/check-messaging-token.mjs`: explicit read-only CLI boundary and testable maintenance orchestration.
- `.github/workflows/check-messaging-token.yml`: action validation and step-scoped read-only versus maintenance execution.
- `scripts/__tests__/instagram-token-workflows.test.mjs`: runtime, exhaustive invariant, CLI and workflow regressions.
- `docs/INSTAGRAM_TOKEN_SETUP.md`: distinct messaging modes, safe revision selection, rollback cautions and Meta-confirmed Instagram Login introspection limitation.
- `docs/catalog-persistence/catalog-list-decisions.json`: one evidence-backed review of the `ok` / `expiringSoon` boolean test-result keys; no bulk approval or report regeneration.

## Local validation and diagnostic history

- Node `22.14.0`, committed npm lockfile: `npm ci` passed. Pinned mobile submodule `790e03e1fb19083a92c2828a8b77ba1016fd53e4` initialized unchanged.
- `node --test scripts/__tests__/instagram-token-workflows.test.mjs`: 24/24 passed.
- `npm run quality:repo`: passed repository-generated artifact verification, formal/model checks, loop regressions, production-release checks, CI-pipeline tests, token tests and persona-program validation.
- `node --test scripts/__tests__/catalog-list-audit.test.mjs`: 2/2 passed.
- After synchronization: the strict catalog audit passed with 1,111 reviewed / zero unreviewed / zero stale decisions; `npm run quality:repo` passed again, the token suite passed 24/24 on the final tree, and focused release-artwork tests passed 13/13 in two suites. Dependency manifests and lockfiles did not change.
- `./node_modules/.bin/audit-ci --config ./audit-ci.jsonc`: passed the unchanged security policy.
- `node --check scripts/check-messaging-token.mjs`, YAML syntax parse and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Direct CLI negative check with messaging/app credential variables explicitly removed: exited 1 and reported no credentials changed, as required. No real provider call or Fly operation was made.
- Before implementation, the new manual-check regression failed against the old workflow. The first catalog attempt was premature while npm installation was incomplete; the later completed audit identified exactly one new candidate, reviewed individually from the source. A new subprocess-based CLI test timed out starting Node on the busy host. It was replaced with assertions against the actual CLI entry function, preserving argument rejection and exit-code coverage without relaxing a timeout or removing the safety assertion. The complete repository suite then passed.

## Expected conditional skips

On manual `check`, Fly CLI installation and credential maintenance must skip: the replacement read-only step runs the same existing token health inspection and fails if maintenance is required. On schedule/`refresh`, the read-only step skips and existing maintenance runs. Success skips failure notification.

This five-file automation/documentation change does not modify application code, schemas, clients or dependencies. The repository's unchanged path classifier selected repository quality and legitimately skipped the separate UI/mobile/backend/contract-test/migration-test jobs on ordinary PR CI; all aggregate gates succeeded. Safe-install independently ran the complete UI tests and production build, and persona journeys ran. No skipped job is claimed to have executed. No triggers, matrices, thresholds, checks or security policy were weakened.

## Security, compatibility and rollback

No credential change, token exchange, Fly update, production deployment or data migration is authorized or performed by this follow-up. No API/schema compatibility change is introduced. Existing scheduled refresh semantics and token health policy remain unchanged; this PR separates side effects rather than claiming a new provider metadata policy.

Use manual checks only on a reviewed ref containing this implementation. Old revisions silently ignore `--check` and can mutate credentials. Reverting the PR restores that old behavior; stop using manual checks on reverted revisions. Reverting code cannot undo a separately authorized credential update.

## Remaining external blocker

This PR does not resolve the separate Instagram Login debugger failure: [run 34922343353](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34922343353) passed account access but failed metadata inspection with HTTP 400/API code 2. A fresh browser tab successfully read the response in [confidential Meta case #1978991836117141](https://developers.facebook.com/support/bugs/1978991836117141/): Meta closed the case after confirming that Facebook's debugger does not reliably support Instagram Login tokens, that changing inspector app credentials will not resolve it, and that no equivalent documented read-only introspection endpoint is available. This is an unsupported integration, not a proven global outage.

Meta recommended its Developer Portal Access Token Debugger. The tool was opened without entering a token; its ability to inspect the current credential remains unverified. The authorized account operator needs the original securely retained token, since GitHub Actions secrets cannot be retrieved. If no copy exists, a new explicitly approved credential flow is needed; do not generate or rotate credentials merely to manufacture passing checks. Preserve validity, app ownership and authoritative expiry validation when designing any replacement. GitHub scope: repository Actions secret `INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`; no Fly secret/deployment changes authorized. After a supported replacement and its regression coverage are reviewed, rerun the nonmutating `action=check` and verify all validation stages succeed. The broader CI audit remains blocked on this requirement.

Full original root-cause, migration, generated-client and main-build evidence remains in #333. Its successful main runs do not substitute for fresh validation of this PR.

## Final scope checkpoint

The refreshed inventory contains 37 open PRs. Initial-scope #331 remains OPEN and MERGEABLE at `25416b43eb8a24b2a57a180fbb846d9db8addcb1`, with all 17 reported checks successful at the last direct check. Later PRs were not added to the original audit scope or modified.

This follow-up is **fixed and verified on the correction PR, with renewed human review required**. Main `52b32e4` passed Catalog, Safe Install and Datadog; the earlier scheduled messaging, enrichment dry-run and full Build Image successes are on `73edd77a`, not the current SHA. The existing Build Image push filter correctly did not trigger for the UI-only artwork change; no filter was changed. Main's old manual-check implementation remains until this PR is merged. The distinct Instagram Login metadata workflow is still **blocked by the external requirement** described above; the overall original objective is not claimed complete. External preview results are reported through GitHub; provider-internal logs were not audited here.
